biography.plain_text: Jacques Lejeune was a French paper industrialist and investor based in Geneva. He built his fortune in paper production and distribution, owning a substantial interest in Alicel before its sale in 1991. He subsequently invested in tobacco and special steels, having also chaired the Soparges paper group during his earlier industrial career.

long_biography.plain_text:
When the Alizay pulp mill came up for sale, Jacques Lejeune assembled a shareholder group to buy it. He was then general manager of the Pont-Sainte-Maxence paper works. The resulting Alicel company brought his Soparges-Mafipa interests together with the Swedish producer MoDo, which held a minority stake.

Under that ownership, the plant underwent a staged modernisation: wood handling, cooking and washing were improved before attention turned to bleaching and energy equipment. The wood-yard control room became fully automated. A new recovery boiler and turbine increased the site's capacity to generate electricity from steam, while plans for an adjoining paper-making operation progressed.
